study type: Repeated cross-sectional study (secondary analysis of survey data)
exposure: Socioeconomic characteristics (e.g., wealth status, education, manual labor)
Health system factors (e.g., 4ANC visits, maternity incentive use)
outcome: Uptake of at least four antenatal care (4ANC) visits
First postnatal care (PNC) within 48 hours of childbirth
Completion of all three routine visits (4ANC, institutional delivery, 1st PNC)
cohort: The study participants were women aged 15-49 in Nepal who had at least one live birth prior to each of the three Nepal Demographic and Health Surveys.
finding: The study found low completion rates for comprehensive maternity care, significant care discontinuity, increased institutional and private C-section deliveries from 2011 to 2022, and persistent inequities in maternal health service utilization influenced by socioeconomic, marginalization, and geographic factors.
mod_finding: The study identified an increasing trend in institutional deliveries, specifically C-section deliveries in private health facilities, and higher odds of CS among older women, Maithili native speakers, and in provinces with higher overall institutional deliveries.
